persons.name: Kristen Chase
persons.harm: Died of heatstroke at the Challenger Foundation Youth Wilderness program in Utah in 1990, age 16.

contacts.what_institution_did: The owner was charged with negligent homicide and child abuse; he was acquitted on all five charges.
contacts.quote: 16-year-old Kristen Chase, who died from heatstroke at the Challenger Foundation Youth Wilderness. program in Utah in 1990. As a result of her death, the program's owner was charged with negligent homicide, which is a Class A misdemeanor and child abuse. However, he was acquitted and found not guilty on all five charges.
contacts.notes: Background case narrated by host from sources.

persons.outcome_quote: 16-year-old Kristen Chase, who died from heatstroke at the Challenger Foundation Youth Wilderness. program in Utah in 1990. As a result of her death, the program's owner was charged with negligent homicide, which is a Class A misdemeanor and child abuse. However, he was acquitted and found not guilty on all five charges.
persons.notes: Background history segment. She died from the harm, so the prosecution is recorded but outcome is not_protected.

persons.name: Aaron Bacon
persons.harm: Died at 16 of acute peritonitis at North Star Expeditions in Utah in 1994; the show says it resulted from negligence and lack of medical attention.
persons.perpetrator_role: owners and staff of North Star Expeditions

contacts.what_institution_did: Owners and staff were charged; three pled guilty to negligent homicide and another was convicted of felony abuse or neglect and jailed.
contacts.quote: Several staff members at North Star, including owners [perpetrator] and [perpetrator], were charged with abuse and neglect after Aaron's death. [perpetrator], [perpetrator], and staff member [perpetrator] pled guilty to negligent homicide. Another staffer, [perpetrator], was found guilty of felony abuse or neglect of a disabled child and sentenced to a year in jail and 36 months probation.

persons.outcome_quote: Aaron Bacon died from acute peritonitis at North Star Expeditions, Inc. in Utah. Although the death was medically considered natural causes, it was a result of negligence and lack of medical attention.
persons.notes: Background history. Died from the harm, so the convictions are not protection of him.

persons.name: Lulu
persons.harm: Signed into Kids of North Jersey by her parents at 13 in 1984 and held there 13 years, until 26, subjected to kidnappings, beatings, forced labor and mental abuse; held down on the floor for hours.
persons.perpetrator_role: the Kids of North Jersey program and its founders

contacts.institution: State of New Jersey and other state officials
contacts.what_institution_did: The state sued the program's founder for $1 million in Medicaid overbilling and Kids was shut down, along with his programs in other states.
contacts.quote: Two years later, the state of New Jersey sued [perpetrator] for $1 million in Medicaid overbillings, and kids was officially shut down. State officials also shut down the [perpetrator]'s other various programs in California, Florida, and Utah
contacts.notes: Action was for billing fraud, not her abuse specifically.

contacts.what_was_asked: damages from the founder, his wife and an assistant director
contacts.what_institution_did: She sued through her attorney; she was awarded $6.5 million.
contacts.quote: Ultimately, Lulu was awarded a $6.5 million settlement.

persons.outcome_quote: In August 1997, Lulu finally escaped the kids' program.
persons.notes: Name given variously as Lulu Porter/Quarter/Corder. The harm ended when she escaped, not through an institution, so the later closure and civil award are recorded as contacts but outcome is not_protected. Expert Maia Szalavitz also describes her case.

persons.name: Danielle Bregoli
persons.harm: Referred at 13 (2016) by a TV talk show to Turnabout Ranch in Utah; reports being taken in the night, handcuffed, sleep and food deprivation, and witnessing restraints and violence against other teens.
persons.perpetrator_role: Turnabout Ranch staff; the TV host who referred her

contacts.institution: the TV talk show/host that referred her (media)
contacts.what_was_asked: an apology to her and other children sent to such programs
contacts.what_institution_did: The host denied responsibility, saying the show has nothing to do with what happens once guests leave the stage.
contacts.quote: we don't have anything to do with what happens with guests once they leave the stage. That's between the parent. and whatever facility they go to, end quote.
contacts.what_happened_next: She went on to advocate with Breaking Code Silence.

persons.outcome_quote: Danielle later reported she was kidnapped in the middle of the night, handcuffed and taken to the isolated Turnabout Ranch.
persons.notes: Background segment; the only institutional response described is the referring show's statement. Name used as the show uses it.

persons.name: Taylor Goodridge

persons.outcome_quote: the parents of 17-year-old Baruch Silvers sued Discovery Ranch Academy, a Utah Teen Treatment Center after he died by suicide there in November 24.

persons.outcome_quote: So I reached a place of learned helplessness.
persons.notes: No report to any outside body described; she later founded Unsilenced.

persons.name: Leanne (mother)
persons.harm: Her mother, an addict, physically hit her and built a false psychiatric narrative (bipolar/BPD) that led to years of unnecessary medication; physical altercation ended her living with her mother.

quotes.quote: It just was so normalized in my house that I thought that's just the way my mom was.

contacts.what_was_asked: to be believed about her mother
contacts.what_institution_did: Adults told her she was making things up; the therapist was on board with her mother's narrative.
contacts.quote: I'm having all these adults tell me that I'm crazy and then I'm making these things up and I start to believe it.
contacts.what_happened_next: She came to believe the abuse hadn't happened.

contacts.institution: her therapist at New Leaf Academy
contacts.what_was_asked: to be believed and protected on calls with her mother

contacts.what_happened_next: She started to be believed; no longer had to communicate with her mother.

persons.outcome_quote: It was then where they stopped making me communicate with her.
persons.decisive_work_quote: She was a big part in recognizing that my mom had an addiction issue.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: during her New Leaf stay, about 3+ months after first program contact
persons.notes: Earlier childhood therapists accepted the mother's narrative but the abuse itself is not described as raised with them. Protection was from contact with the mother; the physical abuse had already ended when she moved to her father.

persons.outcome_quote: I went into trails being around 98 pounds. I came out of trails weighing about 80.

persons.name: Lindy (Adirondack Leadership Expeditions)

contacts.what_was_asked: to tell her parents how horrible it was

persons.outcome_quote: The staff just watched it happen.

contacts.notes: Coded as institution exposing/using her trauma.

persons.outcome_quote: The fact that your trauma was being weaponized against you, it was very hurtful and it was very counterproductive.

persons.outcome_quote: After that incident, I told them I needed to go to the psych ward.

persons.name: Molly (Turning Winds program)

contacts.what_was_asked: to tell her mother the program was not what she thought and get help

contacts.what_institution_did: Interviewed her about working conditions and clothing at the facility; outcome of that inquiry not stated.

coder_notes: Season 24 covers survivors of the so-called troubled teen industry. Coding choices: (1) each program a survivor was placed in is treated as a separate perpetrator and gets its own record when the person describes harm done to them there; family abuse and peer/adult assaults are separate records. (2) Complaints made to the abusing program's own staff (letters, calls, therapists) are coded as contacts, since the program is an institution with a duty to respond; responses such as censoring letters or pre-warning parents that complaints are lies are coded protected_itself. Where no complaint was made at all and the only institution was the program, reached_institution is 'no' with institution_was_abusers. (3) Parents are not institutions; parental disbelief is coded as earlier_disbelief where it explains non-reporting. (4) Background/history cases narrated by the host (Kristen Chase, Aaron Bacon, Lulu, Danielle Bregoli, Trails Carolina death, Taylor Goodridge, Baruch Silvers) are included as records; thinner ones are in others_mentioned. (5) Ep5 and ep9 are expert interviews with no person stories. Ep25 updates contain no S24 survivor case updates; a Season 18 fraud update is coded as one group record. The WCN John Callas crossover appears in the S24 file and was coded. (6) Names of perpetrators/accused (program founders, staff, consultants) and of non-harmed family/staff are replaced with roles or [perpetrator] in quotes. Reading was interrupted three times by usage limits; I resumed from my notes and the exact line positions and read every file to its last line. No unassigned episodes appeared related, so none were opened.
